title: Sales By Representative exports name the Sales Type selection
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Starting screen: Reports > Sales By Representative is open in a desktop browser at least 1024 px wide.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. With all Sales Types selected, export the PDF and the CSV and read the filter line at the top of each.
  2. Select only Parts and Part Sales, export again and read the filter line.
  3. Untick every Sales Type and click Export.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: both read "Sales Type: All".
  • Step 2: both read "Sales Type: Parts, Part Sales".
  • Step 3: "Empty export" shows and no file is made.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10890; story SV-11272 (Story 8, Filter both sales reports by Sales Type); PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 8 (14 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S8-R4, read 19 Oct 2026. Source-verified 19 October 2026. The build is not yet available to check this case against.

The Sales By Representative spec, version 28 (12 Oct 2026, S3-R10 and S14-E3), still makes a file with a "Sales Type: None" line when no option is selected. PRD version 8 (14 Oct 2026) is later and says Export shows "Empty export" and makes no file; this case follows the PRD, which we take as prevailing. The difference is on the product owner's question list.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S8-R4: “The filter line at the top of every PDF and CSV export of Sales By Representative reads the same: "Sales Type: All", or the selected names. With no option selected there is nothing to export: Export shows "Empty export" and makes no file.”

References from Design

Claude design canvas "Splitting Sales Representatives" (https://claude.ai/artifact/8MHqwyffAYtqZ6EccS5RUm), pages 4 and 5 (cited by the story), export read 19 Oct 2026, used for on-screen labels; the look itself is checked in the "Design — how it looks" cases.
